An automobile accident can drastically change your life in a matter of seconds. Just one startling shock. A single crunch, loud. After that, the pain begins. In Houston, back injuries from collisions are frequent. Moreover, they are often very serious. A broken arm and a damaged spine are not the same thing. It may affect sitting, walking, sleeping, and even working. If you are dealing with this kind of injury, you need an experienced Houston personal injury attorney. Schechter, Shaffer & Harris, LLP-Accident & Injury Attorneys has been handling serious back injury cases in Houston for many years. They know what the stakes are. Let’s talk about the special features of these cases and the reasons they require substantial legal resources.

When Your Back Takes the Hit

Your spine is the body’s main support beam. Think of it like the frame of a house. If the frame cracks, everything shifts. In car accidents, the force can cause:

Herniated discs
Spinal fractures
Nerve damage
Soft tissue tears
Spinal cord trauma

Even a “minor” crash can lead to major pain. You may feel fine at first. Adrenaline masks symptoms. A few days later, you can barely get out of bed. Severe back injuries often need surgery, rehab, or long-term care. Some people never fully recover. They live with chronic pain. They miss work. They miss normal life. That loss deserves real compensation.

Houston Roads, Real Risks

Houston traffic is no joke. I-10. The 610 Loop. US-59 at rush hour. It’s a mix of speed, stress, and distracted drivers. Add in delivery vans, oil field trucks, and rideshare cars, and you have real risk. One rear-end crash can snap your spine forward. A side impact can twist your back hard. The physics are brutal. Texas law allows injured victims to seek damages if another driver caused the crash. But proving a severe back injury claim is not simple. Here’s the thing. Insurance companies do not like big claims. And severe back injuries often mean big numbers.

The Hidden Cost of Severe Back Injuries

Medical bills stack up fast. MRI scans. Surgery. Physical therapy. Pain management. But the cost is more than bills. You may lose wages. Maybe your job involves lifting or long hours on your feet. Now you can’t do that. You might need a new role—or no role at all.

There’s also pain and suffering. That phrase sounds vague. It’s not. It includes:

Ongoing pain
Loss of sleep
Stress and anxiety
Loss of normal life activities

If you can’t pick up your child or play weekend ball like before, that matters. It has value under Texas law.

Proving a Car Accident Claim in Texas

Texas follows a modified comparative fault rule. If you are more than 50% at fault, you cannot recover damages. If you are less than 51% at fault, your award is reduced by your share of blame. So proof is everything.

You must show:

The other driver owed you a duty of care.
They breached that duty.
The breach caused the crash.
The crash caused your back injury.

That last point is where fights happen. Insurance adjusters often argue that your back problem was “pre-existing.” Maybe you had mild back pain before. They will try to pin everything on that. A strong legal team gathers medical records, expert opinions, crash reports, and even accident reconstruction data. They build a clear story. One that ties the crash to your injury in plain terms. Let me explain something important. Even if you had a prior back issue, you can still recover. Texas law allows claims if the accident made the condition worse. The key is medical proof.

Insurance Companies Play Hardball

You know what? Insurance companies are not in the business of writing big checks.

They may:

Offer a quick, low settlement
Question your medical treatment
Claim your injury is not that serious
Delay the process to wear you down

It can feel personal. It’s not. It’s a strategy. Severe back injury cases often require expert doctors. Sometimes life care planners are involved. These professionals explain future medical needs and long-term limits. Without a lawyer, it is easy to settle for less than your case is worth.

Why a Houston Personal Injury Lawyer Matters

A Houston personal injury lawyer does more than file papers. They protect your claim from the start.

They:

Investigate the crash
Preserve key evidence
Work with medical experts
Calculate full damages
Handle all contact with insurers
Take the case to trial if needed

Schechter, Shaffer & Harris, LLP – Accident & Injury Attorneys has built a strong name in Houston for handling serious injury cases. They know local courts. They know how insurers think. And they know how to present severe back injury cases to juries. Honestly, that experience matters when your future is on the line.

What to Do After a Car Accident with a Back Injury

If you have been in a crash, take these steps:

Seek medical care right away. Even if the pain seems mild.
Follow your doctor’s treatment plan.
Keep records of bills and missed work.
Avoid giving recorded statements without legal advice.
Speak with a Houston personal injury lawyer as soon as possible.

The majority of auto accident claims in Texas have a two-year statute of limitations. The date of the crash is when that clock begins to run. Your case may suffer if you wait. Evidence dwindles. Observers forget. It occurs quickly.

Severe Back Injuries and Long-Term Impact

With time, some back injuries get better. Some stay behind. Partial or total paralysis may result from spinal cord injuries. Long-lasting nerve pain can result from disc injuries. Years later, some victims require additional surgeries. For this reason, the settlement value should account for future expenses as well as current bills. Consider it similar to fixing a roof following a storm. You don’t just patch one shingle and call it a day. The entire structure is fixed by you. Here, the same concept is applicable. A compelling claim considers the impact over a person’s lifetime.

A Local Firm That Knows Houston

Schechter, Shaffer & Harris, LLP – Accident & Injury Attorneys has served injured Texans for decades. Their focus includes serious car crashes and spinal injuries. They approach cases with care but also grit. That mix matters. Clients often say they feel heard. And they feel prepared. Back injury cases are not small claims. They require detailed work and steady guidance. Having a local Houston firm makes communication easier and court appearances smoother. When your back is injured, your routine changes. Your sleep changes. Your work changes. Legal practice support should not add stress. It should ease it.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. What is the value of a back injury case in a Houston auto accident?

Numerous factors affect the value. These consist of pain levels, future care, lost wages, and medical expenses. Higher settlements are frequently the consequence of severe injuries that necessitate surgery or result in long-term harm. Every case is different. To determine fair value, a lawyer examines expert reports and medical records.

2. What if I had a back issue prior to the collision?

You still have time to submit a claim. You might be able to get compensation if the accident made your condition worse. Compensation for aggravation of past injuries is permitted by Texas law. In these situations, medical records and physician opinions are crucial.

3. How long does it take to file a claim for a serious back injury?

Months may pass before some cases settle. Some require a year or longer. The injury, length of treatment, and whether the insurer contests fault all play a role. Because doctors need time to evaluate long-term effects, serious back injury claims frequently take longer to process.

4. Will the court hear my case?

Before a trial, many cases are settled. You should still get ready as though it might go to court. When insurance companies are aware that your attorney is prepared for trial, they frequently make better settlement offers. Your lawyer will provide a jury with evidence and medical experts if necessary.

5. What should I not do if I have a back injury from a car accident?

Don’t put off getting medical attention. Don’t disregard medical advice. Don’t share anything about your injury on social media. Additionally, don’t accept a hasty settlement without a legal review. Early offers frequently fall short of what you are actually worth.
